dedupe_keys.name: charging currents and electric fields of satellite cables during a reasonable worst case space weather scenario

description: This dataset gives modelled internal charging of coaxial satellite cables during a reasonable worst case radiation-belt event. It holds the 99th percentile equatorial omnidirectional electron spectra from the AE9 model at different orbits, the equatorial fluxes at different L shells for 1 in 10, 1 in 50 and 1 in 100 year events based on Meredith and others (2023), and the equilibrium charging currents of a coaxial cable versus L shell for a 1 in 100 year event. Further files give the maximum electric field inside the cable dielectric at different L shells, with and without the LANL geostationary worst-case spectrum and for different Kp values that control radiation-induced conductivity. The spectra were run through the Dielectric Internal Charging Threat Assessment Tool (DICTAT) version 4.2. It was prepared by Pak Lam, Richard Horne, Nigel Meredith, Sarah Glauert and Peter Kirsch of the British Antarctic Survey and published as downloadable text files in November 2024 under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Caveats: results are for a generic coaxial geometry and chosen shielding, depend on DICTAT settings, and are model outputs, not on-orbit measurements. It supports electrostatic discharge risk screening for satellite design and fleet-level space weather impact scenarios; a related record is the NS41 GPS-orbit extreme electron fluxes.
